newsitem.title: USA: CME feeder cattle end mostly up, new highs set.
newsitem.headline: CME feeder cattle end mostly up, new highs set.

text.p: CME feeder cattle futures posted new contract highs early in the May, August and November contracts and closed mostly higher despite expectations for a drop in the latest CME feeder cattle index, traders said.
Live cattle drifted to narrowly mixed closes on a lack of direction from the cash cattle market, traders said.
Feeders closed off 0.125 cent per lb to up 0.450 with only May off and August up 0.450 at 76.000 cents after posting a new high of 76.050. May set a new high early of 73.350 cents.
Live cattle ended off 0.075 to up 0.250 cent with June off most at 63.750.
Although the next CME feeder cattle index is expected to be quoted lower, cash feeder cattle prices generally are still trending higher, which underpinned feeder cattle futures.

"We had a lot more cattle come in on our weekly direct sales - and they tend to trade a little cheaper than most of your sale barn cattle," said Tom Tippens, CEO Professional Cattle Consultants. He noted that this will create a short term drop in the index. But the index should rebound based on overall strong cash feeder markets, weakness in corn and good grazing conditions, he said.
Traders said expectations are the next index will be down $0.81 per cwt. The previous CME feeder cattle index was up $0.24 at $72.78, the highest level since February 17, 1995.

Smith Barney bought August late and Prudential Securities bought early. Rand Financials bought May while Refco sold and Cargill Investor Services spread long February live cattle/short May feeders, pit sources said.

Commercial hedge lifting provided early support in live cattle but prices failed to hold as traders voiced concern over the next move in cash. Although June holds a discount to cash and beef prices are seen firming the next couple of weeks, cash cattle prices are projected to ease into the summer as increased fed cattle numbers become market-ready. Funds remained sellers, traders said.

Beef prices on Friday eased to lowest levels since April 14 but retailer demand for beef was seen increasing in early May to fill late May and early June holiday needs. Increased outdoor grilling was expected as temperatures warm in the Midwest, they said.
LIT division of First Options and Cargill Investor Services sold June while locals bought. RBH spread long June/short Augut, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, June volatility was weak on commission house selling of 62 to 64 puts, pit sources added.
